item.text:
**Verdict:** yes, strongly, but the mobilization was centralized, war-skewed, and loyalty-based rather than institutionally pluralist.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level note | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Executive Order on Russia’s development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Putin turned the program into an implementation chain: a unified plan, a spatial-development strategy, a transport-energy-social infrastructure plan through 2036, priority annual budget allocations, and monitoring by the Presidential Executive Office and State Council. | 8B.3; 8B.2; 8B.1 |
| Positive | List of instructions following Presidential Address to the Federal Assembly | President of Russia | 2024-03-30 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/assignments/orders/73759 | Sets measurable deadlines and targets for the bureaucracy and regions, including top-four GDP by PPP, poverty reduction, import substitution, higher R&D, manufacturing growth, and infrastructure repair. That is direct mobilization of the state machine around the chosen agenda. | 8B.3; 8B.2; 8B.1 |
| Positive | Factbox-Putin pledges over $126 billion in public spending as election looms | Reuters via Kelo | 2024-03-11 | https://kelo.com/2024/03/11/factbox-putin-pledges-over-126-billion-in-public-spending-as-election-looms/ | Reuters said Putin promised more than 11.5 trillion roubles in six-year infrastructure and social spending. The same report notes military spending would exceed social spending in 2024, showing that the state apparatus was being mobilized, but toward a war-heavy hierarchy of priorities. | 8B.3; 8B.2 |
| Positive | Putin extends defence ministry purge, hands job to a relative | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-17 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-clears-out-deputy-defence-ministers-appoints-his-relative-3486871 | Putin sacked four deputy defence ministers and brought in loyal replacements, including Anna Tsivileva, Leonid Gornin, Oleg Savelyev, and Pavel Fradkov. Reuters framed this as a push to cut waste, fight corruption, and make the war economy work better. | 8B.3; 8B.2; 7B.5 |
| Positive | Putin appoints Patrushev and Dyumin as Kremlin aides | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-14 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-appoints-patrushev-and-dyumin-as-kremlin-aides/2084276/ | Putin moved long-time insiders and a former bodyguard closer to the center, while keeping Vaino, Gromov, Kiriyenko, and Peskov in place. This shows effective coalition management and consolidation of the ruling network. | 8B.3; 7B.5; 8B.2 |
| Positive | Putin orders Russian army to become second largest after China's at 1.5 million-strong | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-16 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-orders-russian-army-to-grow-by-180000-soldiers-to-become-15-millionstrong-3617373 | Putin ordered the regular army expanded by 180,000 to 1.5 million active servicemen. That is a direct command-level mobilization of military capacity toward the ruler’s war goals. | 8B.3; 8B.2 |
| Mixed | Analysis-Russia's GDP boost from military spending belies wider economic woes | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/analysisrussias-gdp-boost-on-military-spending-belies-wider-economic-woes-3295688 | The economy’s rebound depended heavily on state-funded arms and ammunition production. This shows the mobilization was real and effective for war output, but also that it did not translate into broad civilian welfare gains. | 8B.3; 8B.2 |
| Mixed | Russia’s economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reuters reported broad growth and low unemployment, but explicitly tied much of the expansion to military production. That is evidence of effective wartime mobilization, not balanced peacetime development. | 8B.3; 8B.2 |
| Negative | Putin lets economically significant entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Reducing disclosure makes it easier to hide insider privilege and harder for outsiders to verify execution quality. That weakens the state’s feedback loop, even while it protects the ruling network. | 8B.3; 7B.7; 7B.10 |
| Negative | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says power is concentrated in a small closed circle, transparency is weak, and the Kremlin controls media and suppresses opposition. That supports mobilization through a loyalist vertical, not through open institutional coordination. | 8B.3; 7B.6; 7B.10 |
| Negative | Two more Russian officials arrested in widening military corruption probe | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/two-more-russian-officials-arrested-in-widening-military-corruption-probe-3454644 | The defence apparatus still produced major bribery and fraud cases. That is evidence of some internal cleanup, but also shows the mobilization system was leaky and corruption-prone. | 8B.3; 7B.9; 7B.10 |
| Negative | Russia prepares for further tax rises due to war, Reuters reports | Ukrinform / Reuters | 2024-11-02 | https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3922326-russia-prepares-for-further-tax-rises-due-to-war-reuters.html | War financing was forcing tax rises and cuts in small-business support and education development. That is evidence that the mobilization machine was effective for war, but it crowded out other parts of the program. | 8B.3; 8B.2 |

Search gap: I found strong evidence that Putin’s network, bureaucracy, military, and budget were mobilized effectively around war, sovereignty, and regime control. I did not find comparable evidence of an open, plural, self-correcting mobilization process, or a strong counterexample showing that the apparatus failed to execute his main priorities when he chose them.
